questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have previously studied in the United States and because this had been such a great experience, I was eager to do this again. The last time, I was in the South so this time it made sense to study in a northern state. When choosing the specific area in which I wanted to study, then the academic reputation of Boston was obviously an important factor. Also, Boston made sense to me because I have relatives living close to the city. So overall it seemed like a great match.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, perhaps I overestimated how great living and studying in Boston would be because of my previous experiences with studying in the United States. Looking back on it, perhaps I should have chosen a completely different destination.  This being said, I was still very disappointed with how Boston University uses its students for additional profits. It is a sad development how Universities, such as Boston Univesity, care more about making profits than academic integrity.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Getting to the University and getting checked into the room I had been assigned was not too difficult. The international students' office had done a great job at preparing all the information that was needed so that we had a checklist of things to be completed upon arrival in Boston.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I hardly did not need any assistance when I arrived in Boston. Within the first couple of weeks, I had a few questions regarding the courses that I had chosen and a few technicalities, but they were very well handled by Sage Suorsa who was the program manager for the exchange students at Boston University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Boston University had a lot of online orientation and mandatory online introductory courses that seemed so unnecessary for anyone who is a normal grown up. It seems like such a waste of money for the University to have these courses but I guess it all looks good on paper however unnecessary it may seem for the students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Boston University seemed to have a lot of different options for on campus housing. However one is not necessarily assigned to the type of housing that you choose. So be prepared to pay more than you expect.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Essential options were available and I got one of the more affordable meal plans. Then some of the days I was able to cook in the apartment. However these cooking facilities were in no way impressive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Basically, everything I experienced about housing at Boston University is worth criticizing. Boston University is obviously making a profit through exploiting the fact that international students do not know how to find housing in Boston. I applied for the most affordable housing situation but was assigned to a more expensive type of housing where I was to live in a worn-down room right next to a major interstate and a railway. The noise from this was so bad that I could not open a window and still be able to have a conversation with anyone. Also, there was no way of controlling the temperature in the room meaning that it was mostly too hot or too cold. And because of the traffic just outside, sleeping with a window open was not really an option. But here is the awful part of it; Boston University charged $8730 (about 58 000 DKK) for about 3,5 months of rent. Because I was alone in a foreign country, I did not really feel like I had any alternative but to pay the rent. 
I highly encourage other exchange students to find housing off campus and the ideal situation would be to team up among the exchange students (most likely with the other Danish students) and find an apartment off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
If I could have given the on campus housing a lower score, I would!
Also, one might expect that there would be a lot of social activities planned for students living on campus.  However, this is not what I experienced. My residence assistant hardly did anything to promote social activities at the dorm as it was basically non-existing. So do not feel like you are missing out on a lot of social stuff by living off campus...

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registering for new courses was easy and any student used to the system at the University of Copenhagen should not have any difficulties figuring this out. One can rather easily find general information about the courses and then add the courses to a list of courses prior to the start of the registration process. Then actually registering for courses after the registration opens can be done in a matter of seconds.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university provided a great description of how one should complete the registration process and should any exchange students have any difficulties then the coordinator for the exchange students was very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not at first encounter any difficulties in registering for the classes I wanted, however about a week into the classes I was still missing one of the required immunizations. This meant that I was restricted from registering for any new courses and effectively meant that I could not change courses. When I found out that one of my courses was perhaps a bit irrelevant/too easy then this became somewhat of a problem. Morale of this story: Make sure to stay compliant with any requirements from the University, so that they do not restrict your course registration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: One should familiarize themselves with the system used in the United States for measuring the difficulty of the available courses and one should be aware that the general difficulty of most courses is below the difficulty of similar courses at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses at Boston University was in general below that at the University of Copenhagen. I had registered for one course that I had expected was below the level I was at but it proved to be even less difficult. When concerning mathematics, Americans in my experience have a tendency of focusing on the essentials necessary for understanding theory and applying it in the workplace. It is not really my impression that they care all that much about the details in the theory which is unfortunate because essential theoretical understanding is lost. In my opinion too much emphasis is on the application of theory instead of understanding the underlying more challenging reasoning.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was in some of my classes more like being back in high school in the sense that one had homework for every class, and this had to be handed in. It has been my experience at the University of Copenhagen that students are expected to follow the course material for their own benefit and if one does not keep up with exercises then one will not be prepared for the finals. At Boston University however, since the final grade also depends on your overall participation in the course, then it is also important for professors to have physical evidence of how you perform every week during the course. This results in a lot of dull mandatory exercises were one sometimes waste time on making it presentable instead of being able to focus on the actual theory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CAS HI151 - The Emerging United States to 1865
CAS MA226 - Differential Equations
MET AT751 - Individual Insurance Applications of Actuarial Principles
MET AT762 - Mathematical Finance for Actuarial Science
PDP FT140 - Marathon Training

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Even though the mathematics involved with the course was not at all challenging, I think I would recommend “Individual Insurance Applications of Actuarial Principles” to any student with mathematics who wants to familiarize themselves with life insurance in the United States. This course covers many details about the construction of insurance contracts and aspects of how insurance companies determine reserves.
On a more personal note, I really enjoyed learning about American History prior to 1865 with the philosophy that if one is interested in American history, where better to learn about it than in Boston from American professors?

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was assigned to a different type of housing than I had preferred, and this was more expensive than I had estimated at first in my budget. Any potential exchange student should make themselves aware of how Boston University might assign housing different from what students have requested and one can thereby encounter unexpected extra charges.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I was surprised by how expensive food is in Boston in general. Massachusetts overall has a relatively high sales tax and combined with living expenses just being higher in the city, then general everyday grocery shopping was surprisingly expensive.
Also, as I have already mentioned a couple of times, housing was ridiculously expensive, and one would not be able to look closer at this without realizing how Boston University is exploiting that international students do not have that many alternatives when moving to Boston. Boston University has one purpose and one purpose alone, and this is sadly to maximize its profit.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Boston University had a wide range of activities available for students. During the first week or so they even had an event planned where one could explore all the different clubs at the University. This was a very overwhelming experience but also a great way of getting involved with organizations appropriate for one's interest.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I chose to join the running club which I would recommend other exchange students to consider. Physical training is important for ones physical as well as mental wellbeing, but it is also a great way to make new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Any exchange student in Boston studying there during the fall should explore some of the nature outside of the city when the leaves start to change color. New England in general has a reputation of being gorgeous during the fall.
I spent a weekend in New York with some of the other exchange students. Although it is expensive to be in New York it is an obvious place to visit.
But overall, I would just recommend potential future students to be open to any social event or weekend they may be invited to by fellow students. It is wonderful to interact with local students and one will most likely learn how most of us are not really as different as we sometimes have a tendency to believe that we are.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had previously studied in the United States and so, I pretty much knew what to expect and how it would feel to be speaking one's second language all the time. However, I would note to new students that the overall culture in Boston is in my experience more European than many other places in the United States and so one should not really expect something radically different from when living in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Chat with your fellow classmates and be open for invitations to social events. Also, join a club of your interest! (…Or possibly a fraternity if you are under 21 and have the time for it)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Boston is very European in many ways and so I did not find that many challenging cultural differences. However, one might find that Americans have a slightly different sense of humor in some ways and at times I found that they seemed more immature than I would have expected from my peers back in Denmark.

One very surprising cultural difference I encountered in Boston was that most of my classes mostly consisted of Chinese students. This is especially the case in courses within mathematics.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: One quality that I think we could learn from in Denmark is how Americans reward and celebrate the great achievements. Danes have a tendency of thinking that we should all be the same and therefore nobody is allowed to be recognized as being better at something than others. Americans view the great performance as something to be inspired by and they recognize the great performance without any hint of bitterness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be aware that it is expensive living and studying in Boston so include some extra room in your budget for unexpected expenses.
- Boston University does not in my experience care much for stimulating the social life at the dorms, so be advised that one should find their own social groups. A good way to do this would be to join one of the many clubs at Boston University.
- Follow your classes and keep up with the homework but remember to take the time to explore Boston and make great friendships. In the end, these are the things you most likely will remember.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Personally I would recommend exchange students to communicate a lot throughout their stay and invite each other for different social events. It may be great to make some local friendships in Boston, but it may be even more rewarding to make friendships all around the globe.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Find a goal that you want to achieve and do your best to succeed. For me it was running a Marathon and I accomplished this after many practices in the running club and having joined a marathon running class.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it challenging to accept how Boston University as an institution did not care for its students but only for maximizing profits. Luckily, I managed to set this somewhat aside and enjoy the time I had in Boston. I had some interesting classes with great professors and also made some great experiences and friendships.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do not live on campus. Find housing off campus with the other exchange students!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
